newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Borsodchem hits new high on mixed Budapest.
newsitem.headline: Borsodchem hits new high on mixed Budapest.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mixed on Wednesday and traders said there was no apparent impact of the nervousness which drove down other markets ahead of Wall Street's opening.
"Several bourses went down today and they had apparently no effect on the Hungarian market," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities.
The BUX index rose 13.05 points, finishing at 3,798.03, just below the all-time high of 3,803.45 points.
Traders said the rise of the BUX index was due mainly to the price increase of oil and gas company MOL.
"Overall, MOL was the only one which could substantially improve," Lencs said. MOL peaked at 1,945 forints, before retreating to close at 1,930, up 80.
"MOL has been rising almost continuously since the announcement of energy price increase," he said.
"I think the impact of the energy price increase can explain MOL's rise,"

The Hungarian government announced in late November that it would increase retail gas prices by 18.8 percent and electricity prices by 24.9 percent from January 1, 1997. The increases had been postponed from October.
Elsewhere on the market the chemical firms traded actively with rising prices.
Borsodchem rose to an all-time high of 3,760 forints, before closing at 3,750 forints, up 100. TVK edged up five forints to finish at 1,635.

Hotelier Danubius grabbed attention when trading in its shares was suspended for the day because the company was unable to comment on press reports that the Competition Office had approved the company's purchase of Hungaria Szalloda.
Competition Office officials confirmed the news to Reuters.
"Danubius may edge up on Thursday but I don't expect it to rally," Lencs said, adding that market participants already factored in the positive news on the level of expectations.
Trading was suspended also in frozen food maker Goldsun after an unacceptably rapid intraday price fall. The suspension came when Goldsun shares traded at 60 forints, a new all-time low.
